Component: SwiftMailer (mail transport bundled by legacy Laravel 4.x/5.0) — NOT Laravel core
Summary: [SwiftMailer package CVE (<5.4.5), NOT Laravel core. Needs old Laravel with sendmail transport plus attacker-controlled From. No lab present.] SwiftMailer sendmail argument-injection RCE
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: SwiftMailer <= 5.4.4 (as used by a PHP/Laravel mail transport)
Trigger: a reachable mail-send endpoint passes attacker-controlled From/Sender/Return-Path into the SwiftMailer sendmail transport
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: app-sink-required
Vulnerable Lab: No dedicated lab (SwiftMailer package CVE; not reproducible against stock Laravel)

Component: Laravel PendingBroadcast deserialization POP chain
Summary: A deserialization vulnerability in the destruct() function of Laravel v8.5.9 allows attackers to execute arbitrary commands.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: laravel/framework <= 8.5.9 (provides the PendingBroadcast __destruct POP gadget)
Trigger: the application calls unserialize() on attacker-controlled input at a reachable route
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: app-sink-required
Mitigation Steps: There is no upstream laravel/framework patch for this CVE, and none is expected: PendingBroadcast::__destruct() is a Property-Oriented-Programming (POP) gadget, not a bug. The destructor still calls $this->events->dispatch($this->event) verbatim on the current 8.x HEAD, and the gadget remains a live phpggc Laravel/RCE chain across Laravel 6.x/7.x/8.x. The real vulnerability is an APPLICATION-level unserialize() of attacker-controlled input; upgrading Laravel alone does NOT fix it (the framework only supplies the gadget).

Component: Laravel Ignition execute-solution/log poisoning RCE
Summary: Ignition before 2.5.2, as used in Laravel and other products, allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code because of insecure usage of file_get_contents() and file_put_contents(). This is exploitable on sites using debug mode with Laravel before 8.4.2.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: facade/ignition <= 2.5.1 (shipped by Laravel < 8.4.2)
Trigger: APP_ENV != production AND APP_DEBUG=true (registers POST /_ignition/execute-solution)
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: config-dependent
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade facade/ignition to a patched release: >= 2.5.2 (also backported to 2.4.2, 1.16.14, and 1.6.15); on Laravel this corresponds to upgrading to Laravel >= 8.4.2. Patch adds isSafePath() in MakeViewVariableOptionalSolution, which requires viewFile to start with '/' or './' and end in '.blade.php', blocking php://filter / phar:// stream wrappers and non-blade targets. Config-level mitigation without upgrading: set APP_DEBUG=false (and ensure APP_ENV=production) so the unauthenticated /_ignition/execute-solution route is not registered/exposed; this fully closes the attack surface since the chain requires Ignition's debug endpoints to be reachable.
Fix ref: https://github.com/facade/ignition/commit/11ffca14abd22db779d90b12e193f8000f6d184b

Component: Laravel upload validation allowing executable PHP/.phar content
Summary: Laravel Framework through 8.70.2 does not sufficiently block the upload of executable PHP content because Illuminate/Validation/Concerns/ValidatesAttributes.php lacks a check for .phar files, which are handled as application/x-httpd-php on systems based on Debian. NOTE: this CVE Record is for Laravel Framework, and is unrelated to any reports concerning incorrectly written user applications for image upload.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: laravel/framework <= 8.70.2
Trigger: upload endpoint uses the mimes:jpg,jpeg,png,gif rule and stores accepted files under their original name in a web-served, .phar-executing directory
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: config-dependent
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade to Laravel Framework 8.73.0 (8.x) or 6.20.41 (6.x), which add 'phar' to the shouldBlockPhpUpload() blocklist so the mimes/mimetypes validators reject .phar uploads. Defense-in-depth at the application level (independent of framework version): store uploads outside any web-/PHP-executable directory and never serve user uploads through mod_php, and validate by verified content/MIME rather than trusting the client-supplied extension.…
Fix ref: https://github.com/laravel/framework/commit/2d1f76ab752ced011da05cf139799eab2a36ef90

Component: UniSharp laravel-filemanager upload RCE
Summary: UniSharp Laravel Filemanager upload RCE: a valid MIME type plus a trailing dot after a .php extension (e.g. shell.php.) bypasses the extension blocklist, allowing a webshell upload and code execution.
Auth/Privilege Required: Depends on deployment: None for a stock/unauthenticated laravel-filemanager mount (unauth package harness); Administrator session required where the host app gates the sink (S-Cart admin/admin; Badaso admin@badaso.test with the browse_file_manager permission).
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated) by CVE class; the S-Cart/Badaso app labs gate the upload behind auth
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: unisharp/laravel-filemanager < 2.9.1
Trigger: laravel-filemanager upload reachable and uploads stored under a PHP-executing web path (/storage or /data)
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: config-dependent
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade unisharp/laravel-filemanager to >= 2.9.1, which adds InvalidExtensionException and LfmUploadValidator::extensionIsValid() (regex /[^a-zA-Z0-9]/ rejecting non-alphanumeric extension chars such as the trailing dot in shell.php.) and wires the check into LfmPath::validateUploadedFile(). The advisory-referenced canonical fix is commit 8170760c0ae316d77b9363cd4c76ab68d3f63f0b ('fix(security): file extension should not contain special characters')…
Fix ref: https://github.com/UniSharp/laravel-filemanager/commit/8170760c0ae316d77b9363cd4c76ab68d3f63f0b

Component: Akaunting authenticated locale OS command-injection RCE
Summary: Akaunting <= 3.1.3: module install shells out the artisan command 'module:install {alias} {company_id} {locale}' via Symfony Process::fromShellCommandline() (App\Utilities\Console::run SHELL form => injectable). The company locale is trailing+unquoted. The WIZARD company-update (App\Http\Requests\Wizard\Company::rules()) declares rules for logo/api_key ONLY — no rule for locale — so an authenticated user poisons company.locale with shell metacharacters via POST /{company_id}/wizard/companies and detonates it via POST /{company_id}/apps/install -> RCE. Fixed in 3.1.4 (validates locale on company-update).
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: authenticated (admin / company-manager)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: Akaunting <= 3.1.3
Trigger: poison company `locale` with shell metacharacters via POST /{company}/wizard/companies, then detonate via POST /{company}/apps/install
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: realistic
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade akaunting/akaunting to 3.1.4 or later (validate locale on company-update).
Fix ref: https://github.com/akaunting/akaunting

Component: InvoiceShelf/Crater cookie-session deserialization RCE
Summary: Crater / InvoiceShelf unauth deserialization RCE: with SESSION_DRIVER=cookie and a known APP_KEY, the laravel_session cookie is re-encrypted with tampered serialized data, triggering deserialization to RCE.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: required
Affected: InvoiceShelf <= 1.3.0 (patched 2.0.0); Crater <= 6.0.6
Trigger: SESSION_DRIVER=cookie (encrypted session carries serialized PHP) and a valid APP_KEY is known/recovered; OOB HTTP callback used for command proof
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: config-dependent
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade InvoiceShelf to 2.0.0 or later (fix commit a64701bda570629757d3dd5a9277584fc0aeb34c sets SESSION_DRIVER=file by default); affected Crater <= 6.0.6. Without upgrading, fully mitigate by setting SESSION_DRIVER to any non-cookie driver (file/database/redis) in your .env so serialized PHP never travels in the cookie, AND rotate APP_KEY to a unique secret value (do not keep the shipped default base64:kgk/4DW1vEVy7aEvet5FPp5un6PIGe/so8H0mvoUtW0=). Either of these alone breaks the exploit — non-cookie driver removes the unserialize-from-cookie path, and a secret APP_KEY makes the encrypted/HMAC'd cookie unforgeable.
Fix ref: https://github.com/InvoiceShelf/InvoiceShelf/commit/a64701bda570629757d3dd5a9277584fc0aeb34c

Component: livewire-filemanager/filemanager unrestricted PHP upload RCE
Summary: Livewire Filemanager, commonly used in Laravel applications, contains LivewireFilemanagerComponent.php, which does not perform file type and MIME validation, allowing for RCE through upload of a malicious php file that can then be executed via the /storage/ URL if a commonly performed setup process within Laravel applications has been completed.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: livewire-filemanager/filemanager <= 1.0.4 (third-party package, not Laravel core)
Trigger: `php artisan storage:link` in place so uploads are web-served under /storage; filemanager upload reachable
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: config-dependent
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade livewire-filemanager/filemanager to v1.0.5 or later (v1.1.0 also fixed). Note: the GitHub Advisory GHSA-9g95-48c6-r778 and NVD currently list 'Patched versions: None', but this is stale — fix commit 988a6293f013f18a95fffe4b370f42751fae5e6c ('Updated security issue + file validation') is included in the v1.0.5 tag, which adds a rules() mimes allowlist plus a $this->validate() call in updatedFiles(). If you cannot upgrade: (1) the new allowlist is configurable via livewire-filemanager.api.allowed_extensions, so on patched versions tighten/confirm it; (2) at the web-server layer, serve the public storage path (storage/app/public, exposed via storage:link) as static-only / non-executable so an uploaded .php cannot run…
Fix ref: https://github.com/livewire-filemanager/filemanager/commit/988a6293f013f18a95fffe4b370f42751fae5e6c

Component: Pterodactyl Panel unauthenticated RCE via /locales/locale.json traversal and PHP PEAR
Summary: Pterodactyl Panel <= 1.11.10: /locales/locale.json passes attacker-controlled locale and namespace query parameters into Laravel translation FileLoader path construction, allowing traversal into arbitrary PHP files. Exploitation can include PHP PEAR pearcmd.php, write a temporary PHP payload, and include that payload for unauthenticated in-band command execution; the same primitive can disclose APP_KEY and DB config. Patched in 1.11.11 by LocaleRequest validation enforcing locale ^[a-z][a-z]$ and namespace ^[a-z]{1,191}$.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: Pterodactyl Panel <= 1.11.10
Trigger: reach /locales/locale.json traversal; command path additionally needs a reachable PEAR pearcmd.php and register_argc_argv=On
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: config-dependent
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade pterodactyl/panel to 1.11.11 or later, or apply the LocaleRequest validation patch for locale/namespace.
Fix ref:
https://github.com/pterodactyl/panel/commit/24c82b0e335fb5d7a844226b08abf9f176e592f0

Component: Livewire v3 unsafe hydration RCE; Snipe-IT and minimal counter labs
Summary: Livewire is a full-stack framework for Laravel. In Livewire v3 up to and including v3.6.3, a vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote command execution in specific scenarios. The issue stems from how certain component property updates are hydrated. This vulnerability is unique to Livewire v3 and does not affect prior major versions. Exploitation requires a component to be mounted and configured in a particular way, but does not require authentication or user interaction. This issue has been patched in Livewire v3.6.4. All users are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version or later as soon as possible. No known workarounds are available.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: authenticated (staff) for the real Snipe-IT sink; unauthenticated by Livewire CVE class
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: Livewire v3, 3.0.0-beta.1 through 3.6.3 (fixed 3.6.4)
Trigger: reach a Livewire v3 component exposing an untyped/weakly-typed public property (hydration type juggling)
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: realistic
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade livewire/livewire to 3.6.4 or later (the fix commit ef04be7 landed in the v3.6.4 tag, where hydratePropertyUpdate() now guards __rm__ removals). The vulnerable range is Livewire v3.0.0-beta.1 through 3.6.3; Livewire v1/v2 are unaffected. No upstream config workaround exists.
Fix ref: https://github.com/livewire/livewire/commit/ef04be759da41b14d2d129e670533180a44987dc

Component: Laravel Reverb Redis scaling deserialization RCE
Summary: Laravel Reverb insecure deserialization RCE: when horizontal scaling is enabled, Reverb consumes Redis Pub/Sub scaling messages and passes that data to unserialize() without a class allowlist. The command trigger is not an HTTP route; HTTP can fingerprint Reverb or read optional lab proof, while RCE proof/output is OOB or side-channel.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: laravel/reverb <= 1.6.3 (fixed 1.7.0)
Trigger: Redis horizontal scaling enabled (REVERB_SCALING_ENABLED=true) and attacker can publish a serialized message to the Redis scaling channel
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: config-dependent
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade laravel/reverb to ^1.7.0, which adds the unserialize allowed_classes allowlist (commit 9ec26f8, PR #360). All versions < 1.7.0 are affected when horizontal scaling is enabled. Config-level mitigation that closes the hole without upgrading: set REVERB_SCALING_ENABLED=false (run a single Reverb node so no untrusted data is unserialized from Redis PubSub), and/or require a strong Redis password and bind Redis to a private/loopback interface so an attacker cannot PUBLISH to the scaling channel.
Fix ref: https://github.com/laravel/reverb/commit/9ec26f8ffbb701f84920dd0bb9781a1797591f1a

Component: Livewire temporary file upload validation bypass
Summary: Livewire is a full-stack framework for Laravel that allows for dynamic UI components without leaving PHP. In livewire/livewire prior to `2.12.7` and `v3.5.2`, the file extension of an uploaded file is guessed based on the MIME type. As a result, the actual file extension from the file name is not validated. An attacker can therefore bypass the validation by uploading a file with a valid MIME type (e.g., `image/png`) and a “.php” file extension. If the following criteria are met, the attacker can carry out an RCE attack: 1. Filename is composed of the original file name using `$file->getClientOriginalName()`. 2. Files stored directly on your server in a public storage disk. 3. Webserver is configured to execute “.php” files. This issue has been addressed in release versions `2.12.7` and `3.5.2`. All users are advised to upgrade. There are no known workarounds for this vulnerability.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: authenticated (low-privilege) per advisory; the lab exposes an unauth /upload for reproduction
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: Livewire < 2.12.7 or v3 < 3.5.2
Trigger: app stores uploads under the original client filename (not Livewire's randomized name) and the upload component is reachable
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: lab-unauth/prod-auth
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade livewire/livewire to 3.5.2 (v3) or 2.12.7 (v2); both releases replace $file->guessExtension() with $file->getClientOriginalExtension() in generateHashNameWithOriginalNameEmbedded(). Config-level mitigation without upgrade: keep uploads on a private, non-web-served disk and never store with the original client filename (Livewire's default randomized hashed name makes the bypass inert), and ensure the webserver does not execute .php files in any public storage path. The GHSA states there are no other known workarounds besides upgrading.
Fix ref: https://github.com/livewire/livewire/commit/70503b7

Component: Laravel wildcard file/image validation bypass
Summary: Laravel is a web application framework. When using wildcard validation to validate a given file or image field (`files.*`), a user-crafted malicious request could potentially bypass the validation rules. This vulnerability is fixed in 11.44.1 and 12.1.1. Also affected: < 10.48.29 (patched in 10.48.29), in addition to 11.x (11.44.1) and 12.x (12.1.1).
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: Laravel 10.0.0-10.48.28, 11.0.0-11.44.0, 12.0.0-12.1.0
Trigger: a wildcard files.* validation rule built from the fluent File rule object (File::types([...])); reach that endpoint
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: config-dependent
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade Laravel framework to a patched release: 10.48.29, 11.44.1, or 12.1.1 (GHSA-78fx-h6xr-vch4). Affected ranges: <10.48.29, >=11.0.0 <11.44.1, >=12.0.0 <12.1.1. Without upgrading, avoid applying wildcard file/image validation (e.g. 'files.*' bound to the fluent Illuminate\\Validation\\Rules\\File rule object such as File::types([...]) / File::image()) to attacker-controlled array uploads; the plain string rules image/mimes are NOT bypassable because they route through shouldBlockPhpUpload().
Fix ref: https://github.com/laravel/framework/commit/2d133034fefddfb047838f4caca3687a3ba811a5

Component: Laravel 5.1 POP gadget chain requiring a custom unsafe unserialize() sink
Summary: Laravel 5.1 gadget-chain report that is only exploitable when an application exposes an unsafe unserialize() sink. The reproducible lab now supplies that sink synthetically at /deserialize, base64-decodes attacker-controlled request parameters, and unserializes the decoded PHP object so the module can prove marker execution and --command execution. Laravel 5.1 presence alone remains insufficient.
Auth/Privilege Required: None in synthetic lab; real targets depend on the app-owned sink exposure.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: Laravel 5.1.0-5.1.46 (incidental; no framework code path or patch)
Trigger: an app-provided unserialize() sink on attacker input (the lab adds a synthetic /deserialize route)
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: disputed (synthetic sink)
Mitigation Steps: Do not call unserialize() on attacker-controlled input. Replace PHP serialization with JSON or signed/validated formats, block object instantiation with allowed_classes=false where legacy deserialization is unavoidable, and upgrade away from obsolete Laravel 5.1 dependencies.

Component: Laravel .env disclosure / APP_KEY and credential leakage
Summary: In Laravel framework through 5.5.21, remote attackers can obtain sensitive information (such as externally usable passwords) via a direct request for the /.env URI. NOTE: this CVE is only about Laravel framework's writeNewEnvironmentFileWith function in src/Illuminate/Foundation/Console/KeyGenerateCommand.php, which uses file_put_contents without restricting the .env permissions. The .env filename is not used exclusively by Laravel framework.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: Laravel 5.5.x deploy/permissions misconfiguration (version-agnostic on the line)
Trigger: web server serves .env / backup env files (docroot is the project root, or dotfiles are served)
Command-capable: no
Scenario: config-dependent
Mitigation Steps: No upstream code patch exists. The NVD-cited file_put_contents()-without-chmod in writeNewEnvironmentFileWith() persists unchanged from v5.5.21 through Laravel v11.0.0 (only error-handling for a missing APP_KEY was later added, not any permission restriction), and GHSA-2v4r-7m2m-5chh lists the patched version as 'Unknown' (unreviewed) with no fix commit/PR references. Laravel's position (consistent with the NVD note that '.env filename is not used exclusively by Laravel framework') is that /.env disclosure is a webserver misconfiguration, not a framework defect.

Component: Laravel encrypted X-XSRF-TOKEN deserialization with known APP_KEY
Summary: In Laravel Framework through 5.5.40 and 5.6.x through 5.6.29, remote code execution might occur as a result of an unserialize call on a potentially untrusted X-XSRF-TOKEN value. This involves the decrypt method in Illuminate/Encryption/Encrypter.php and PendingBroadcast in gadgetchains/Laravel/RCE/3/chain.php in phpggc. The attacker must know the application key, which normally would never occur, but could happen if the attacker previously had privileged access or successfully accomplished a previous attack.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: required
Affected: laravel/framework <= 5.5.40 or 5.6.x <= 5.6.29
Trigger: a known/leaked APP_KEY and a reachable endpoint that decrypts X-XSRF-TOKEN/cookie (Encrypter::decrypt -> unserialize)
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: config-dependent
Mitigation Steps:
Fixed in Laravel Framework v5.6.30 (and the corresponding 5.5 LTS patch). Fix commit c0eb9073eb (PR #25121, \"dont serialize csrf cookie / header\") plus follow-ups 97467e3ca7/240d904606 disable serialization for cookies/headers; the security-critical change is VerifyCsrfToken::getTokenFromRequest() now calling $this->encrypter->decrypt($header, false) so the attacker-controlled X-XSRF-TOKEN is never unserialized. Upgrade to >= 5.6.30 (or the patched 5.5.x).
Fix ref: https://github.com/laravel/framework/commit/c0eb9073eb2cedab1db6c0d1ea4b3aecdc258597

Component: Laravel Filesystem::link() command injection / command sink lab
Summary: OS Command injection vulnerability in function link in Filesystem.php in Laravel Framework before 5.8.17.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: laravel/framework < 5.8.17 (labs reproduce the command-injection class; detector is version-agnostic)
Trigger: a reachable route concatenates attacker input into a shell ln -s (Linux) / mklink (Windows) call without escaping
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: app-sink-required
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade laravel/framework to 5.8.17 or later (fixed by commit 44c3feb604944599ad1c782a9942981c3991fa31, which applies escapeshellarg() to both link() arguments). The vulnerable shell sink only executes on the Windows code path (windows_os() branch using exec(\"mklink ...\")); non-Windows deployments use PHP's native symlink() and are not affected. Regardless of OS, never pass attacker-controlled paths into Storage::link()/Filesystem::link(); validate/whitelist any path arguments at the application layer.
Fix ref: https://github.com/laravel/framework/commit/44c3feb604944599ad1c782a9942981c3991fa31

Component: BookStack image upload (is_image mime-only validation) RCE
Summary: BookStack <= 0.25.2: ImageController::uploadByType() validated uploads with a custom is_image rule checking ONLY the content-derived getMimeType() (magic bytes), not the file extension. A file named shell.php whose bytes start with GIF89a reports image/gif, passes validation, and is stored verbatim under public/uploads/images/.../shell.php (the local disk root IS public_path()) where php-fpm executes it on GET -> RCE. Fixed in 0.25.3 (commit 37b91b6b) by swapping to Laravel's extension-aware mimes: rule.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: authenticated (image-create permission)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: BookStack <= 0.25.2
Trigger: reach the authenticated image-upload endpoint; uploads web-served and PHP-executable
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: realistic
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade bookstack to 0.25.3 or later (extension-aware mimes: validation).
Fix ref: https://github.com/BookStackApp/BookStack/commit/37b91b6b

Component: Laravel Fortify TOTP replay / one-time code reuse
Summary: Laravel Fortify before 1.11.1 allows a valid TOTP code to be reused within the same time window, weakening the one-time property of 2FA. The local lab demonstrates the replay oracle in-band by submitting the same current code twice to /two-factor-challenge.
Auth/Privilege Required: Valid TOTP code/secret; lab self-fetches seeded secret
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated); victim account has TOTP enabled
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: laravel/fortify < 1.11.1
Trigger: Fortify 2FA enabled on the target account; reach the two-factor challenge flow (TOTP capture-replay)
Command-capable: no
Scenario: realistic
Mitigation Steps: Upgrade laravel/fortify to 1.11.1 or later. The fixed release prevents reusing a TOTP code inside the active time window by remembering accepted codes.

Component: Cachet authenticated Twig SSTI (incident-template) — config/APP_KEY disclosure
Summary: Cachet <= 2.3.18: ReportIncidentCommandHandler::parseIncidentTemplate() calls twig->render() un-sandboxed on an attacker-controlled incident-template body. An authenticated user (X-Cachet-Token / dashboard session) injects a Twig payload, then triggers the render via POST /api/v1/incidents {template:<slug>}; the rendered output becomes the incident message, reflected verbatim — an in-band SSTI oracle. On the pinned twig/twig 1.40.1 the command-exec filter-chains do NOT fire, so the DEMONSTRATED primitive is expression-eval + config()/APP_KEY disclosure, not in-band RCE. Fixed in Cachet 2.4 (commit 6fb043e wraps render in a Twig SecurityPolicy sandbox).
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: authenticated (dashboard user able to render incident templates)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: Cachet <= 2.3.18
Trigger: render an incident template (Twig SSTI) to disclose APP_KEY, then forge an X-XSRF-TOKEN deserialization gadget at a CSRF-verified route
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: realistic
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade cachethq/cachet to 2.4 or later (Twig SecurityPolicy sandbox).
Fix ref: https://github.com/cachethq/cachet/commit/6fb043e

Component: Crater superadmin-authenticated upload-logo code-injection RCE
Summary: Crater <= 6.0.6: POST /api/v1/company/upload-logo decodes a JSON company_logo blob {"data":"data:image/png;base64,..","name":"x.php"} and passes the attacker-controlled name straight to spatie/laravel-medialibrary's usingFileName() — CompanyLogoRequest validates only the base64 payload's MAGIC BYTES (Crater\Rules\Base64Mime), never the filename extension. A PNG-magic'd payload named <rand>.php therefore lands web-served and PHP-executable at /storage/{media_id}/<rand>.php -> RCE. Fixed by validating the filename extension.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: authenticated (superadmin, Sanctum)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: Crater <= 6.0.6
Trigger: reach the authenticated logo/upload endpoint; /storage media path web-served and PHP-executable
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: realistic
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade crater-invoice/crater past 6.0.6 (validate filename extension on upload-logo).
Fix ref: https://github.com/crater-invoice/crater

Component: Snipe-IT cookie/session deserialization RCE
Summary: Snipe-IT before 7.0.10 can deserialize attacker-controlled encrypted XSRF-TOKEN cookie data when Passport cookie serialization and EncryptCookies serialize=true are active. With a known, leaked, or default APP_KEY, an unauthenticated attacker can forge the encrypted cookie and trigger a PHP gadget chain for RCE.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: required
Affected: Snipe-IT < 7.0.10
Trigger: Passport cookie serialization + EncryptCookies serialize=true (XSRF-TOKEN plaintext -> unserialize) and a valid APP_KEY to forge the cookie
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: config-dependent
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade Snipe-IT to 7.0.10 or later per NVD/GHSA, and rotate APP_KEY to a unique secret value with php artisan key:generate. Remove/avoid Passport::withCookieSerialization() and never deploy repository default .env APP_KEY values such as base64:3ilviXqB9u6DX1NRcyWGJ+sjySF+H18CPDGb3+IVwMQ=. Rotating APP_KEY immediately breaks forged-cookie exploitation; upgrading removes the cookie serialization sink.
Fix ref: https://github.com/snipe/snipe-it/releases/tag/v7.0.10

Component: Laravel environment/session manipulation with register_argc_argv
Summary: Laravel is a web application framework. When the register_argc_argv php directive is set to on , and users call any URL with a special crafted query string, they are able to change the environment used by the framework when handling the request. The vulnerability fixed in 6.20.45, 7.30.7, 8.83.28, 9.52.17, 10.48.23, and 11.31.0. The framework now ignores argv values for environment detection on non-cli SAPIs.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: laravel/framework < 6.20.45 / 7.30.7 / 8.83.28 / 9.52.17 / 10.48.23 / 11.31.0
Trigger: PHP register_argc_argv=On and attacker can influence the query string (overrides the resolved Laravel environment)
Command-capable: no
Scenario: config-dependent
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade to a patched release: 6.20.45, 7.30.7, 8.83.28, 9.52.17, 10.48.23, or 11.31.0 (the 11.x fix is commit 18b326d2; the 8.x branch fix is commit eded6bdfc05af9b5437d107b4d092558fe46292c — same runningInConsole() gate). The patched framework only consults $_SERVER['argv'] for environment detection when running in the console SAPI. Config-level mitigation without upgrading: set the PHP directive register_argc_argv=Off in php.ini, which stops PHP from populating $_SERVER['argv'] from the query string on web requests and removes the attacker-controllable input entirely.
Fix ref: https://github.com/laravel/framework/commit/18b326d22d831e1fe05e737209e367e30796d5f3

Component: Invoice Ninja route/hash deserialization RCE
Summary: Invoice Ninja pre-auth deserialization RCE: a public route feeds an attacker string to decrypt(); with a known/default APP_KEY the blob is unserialized into a POP chain, yielding unauthenticated RCE.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: required
Affected: Invoice Ninja < 5.10.43 (validated exploitable 5.8.22-5.10.10)
Trigger: reach the route/hash endpoint that accepts encrypted Laravel payloads and a valid APP_KEY to forge the payload
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: config-dependent
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade Invoice Ninja to 5.10.43+, where the official fix (commit d9302021472c3e7e23bac8c3d5fbec57a5f38f0c, "unwind route hash") comments out the vulnerable GET /route/{hash} route in routes/client.php. The vulnerable range is < 5.10.43 (Metasploit-confirmed exploitable >= 5.8.22 and <= 5.10.10). Exploitation strictly requires knowledge of the secret APP_KEY because decrypt() verifies the AES-256-CBC + HMAC envelope before unserialize(); therefore the load-bearing config mitigation is to rotate APP_KEY to a strong unique value stored in a secret manager and never ship the default/committed key (e.g. base64:RR++yx2rJ9kdxbdh3+AmbHLDQu+Q76i++co9Y8ybbno=, which is the Metasploit module default).
Fix ref: https://github.com/invoiceninja/invoiceninja/commit/d9302021472c3e7e23bac8c3d5fbec57a5f38f0c

Component: Laravel Pulse authenticated Livewire remember() RCE
Summary: Laravel Pulse is a real-time application performance monitoring tool and dashboard for Laravel applications. A vulnerability has been discovered in Laravel Pulse prior to version 1.3.1 that could allow remote code execution through the public `remember()` method in the `Laravel\Pulse\Livewire\Concerns\RemembersQueries` trait. This method is accessible via Livewire components and can be exploited to call arbitrary callables within the application. An authenticated user with access to Laravel Pulse dashboard can execute arbitrary code by calling any function or static method in which the callable is a function or static method and the callable has no parameters or no strict parameter types. The vulnerable to component is `remember(callable $query, string $key = '')` method in `Laravel\Pulse\Livewire\Concerns\RemembersQueries`, and the vulnerability affects all Pulse card components that use this trait. Version 1.3.1 contains a patch.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: authenticated
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: Laravel Pulse < 1.3.1
Trigger: reach the Pulse dashboard and influence the remembered query key / Livewire state into the decrypt/unserialize sink
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: config-dependent
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade laravel/pulse to 1.3.1 or later (confirmed: v1.3.1 src/Livewire/Concerns/RemembersQueries.php declares remember() as protected). The fix is a single one-line visibility change (public -> protected) in commit d1a5bf2 / PR #429. No config-only mitigation fully closes the hole, but because exploitation requires an authenticated, authorized Pulse dashboard session, restricting/locking down the viewPulse Gate (e.g. admin-only) and keeping Pulse off in production until patched substantially reduces exposure.
Fix ref: https://github.com/laravel/pulse/commit/d1a5bf2eca36c6e3bedb4ceecd45df7d002a1ebc

Component: Laravel Eloquent mass assignment unsafe create/update flow
Summary: An issue was discovered in Laravel before 6.18.34 and 7.x before 7.23.2. Unvalidated values are saved to the database in some situations in which table names are stripped during a mass assignment.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: laravel/framework < 6.18.34 or 7.x < 7.23.2
Trigger: a mass-assignment route with an app-layer bare-name input filter on a sensitive column; a table-qualified key (users.is_admin) defeats the filter (table-name stripping)
Command-capable: no
Scenario: realistic
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade laravel/framework to 6.18.34 or 7.23.2 (Otwell advisory, 2020-08-06), which makes removeTableFromKey() throw a LogicException for table-qualified (dotted) keys when the model uses a non-empty $guarded (not ['*']). Config-level mitigation without upgrade: declare an explicit $fillable allow-list on sensitive models — a table-prefixed key like 'users.role' is dropped by fillableFromArray()'s array_intersect_key against $fillable, so apps relying solely on $fillable on the bare attribute were never vulnerable.…
Fix ref: https://github.com/laravel/framework/commit/9240404b22ef6f9e827577b3753e4713ddce7471

Component: Laravel Eloquent guarded JSON/nested attribute mass-assignment behavior
Summary: An issue was discovered in Laravel before 6.18.35 and 7.x before 7.24.0. The $guarded property is mishandled in some situations involving requests with JSON column nesting expressions.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: laravel/framework < 6.18.35 or 7.x < 7.24.0
Trigger: an Eloquent model uses $guarded (not $fillable) listing individual columns; reach a mass-assignment sink
Command-capable: no
Scenario: disputed
Mitigation Steps:
Upgrade laravel/framework to 6.18.35 (6.x) or 7.24.0 (7.x), which add isGuardableColumn() schema validation in isGuarded(). Config-level mitigation without upgrade: use an explicit $fillable allow-list instead of $guarded (a $fillable model only mass-assigns enumerated columns and is immune), or set $guarded = [] / ['*'] (only models that enumerate individual columns in $guarded are vulnerable per the advisory). Also ensure routes never pass raw request()->all() straight into create/update/fill.
Fix ref: https://github.com/laravel/framework/commit/897d107775737a958dbd0b2f3ea37877c7526371

Component: Laravel laravel.log database credential disclosure
Summary: A disputed Laravel Framework CVE describing database credential disclosure through publicly readable storage/logs/laravel.log. Treat as a confirmed finding only when the log is web-accessible and contains cleartext DB credential evidence, such as DB_PASSWORD/DB_USERNAME pairs or PDO->__construct() username/password arguments.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: disputed record (Laravel 8-11); exposure is deploy-dependent, not version-specific
Trigger: storage/logs/laravel.log (or equivalent) is web-readable AND contains cleartext DB credentials
Command-capable: no
Scenario: disputed
Vulnerable Lab: No dedicated lab; covered by default log_exposure and CVE wrapper modules/cves/cve_2024_29291.py
Mitigation Steps: Serve Laravel from public/ only, block storage/logs from the web, rotate any exposed database credentials, and reduce sensitive exception logging.

Component: Laravel 5.1 POP gadget chain requiring a custom unsafe unserialize() sink
Summary: Laravel 5.1 gadget-chain report that is only exploitable when an application exposes an unsafe unserialize() sink. The reproducible lab now supplies that sink synthetically at /deserialize, base64-decodes attacker-controlled request parameters, and unserializes the decoded PHP object so the module can prove marker execution and --command execution. Laravel 5.1 presence alone remains insufficient.
Auth/Privilege Required: None in synthetic lab; real targets depend on the app-owned sink exposure.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: none (unauthenticated)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: Laravel 5.1.0-5.1.46 (per NVD/VulDB; duplicate of CVE-2022-2870)
Trigger: an app-provided unserialize() sink on attacker input (the lab adds a synthetic /deserialize route)
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: disputed (synthetic sink)
Mitigation Steps: Do not call unserialize() on attacker-controlled input. Replace PHP serialization with JSON or signed/validated formats, block object instantiation with allowed_classes=false where legacy deserialization is unavoidable, and upgrade away from obsolete Laravel 5.1 dependencies.

Component: Laravel remember-me timing side channel (DatabaseUserProvider)
Summary: Laravel before 5.5.10 compares remember-me tokens with a non-constant-time strcmp in DatabaseUserProvider::retrieveByToken, enabling a timing oracle that can leak valid remember tokens and hijack sessions; chainable to post-auth RCE when weak upload sinks exist.
Exploit Pre-conditions:
Auth: operator-supplied credentials or remember-me token material (no built-in default)
APP_KEY: not required
Affected: laravel/framework < 5.5.10
Trigger: app uses DB remember-me tokens and exposes a post-auth upload sink; reach /login + the upload path
Command-capable: yes
Scenario: partial
Mitigation Steps: Upgrade laravel/framework to v5.5.10 or later so remember-token validation uses hash_equals() in the Auth providers. Defense-in-depth for the lab chain: block PHP execution in user-upload directories and remove unsafe post-auth upload sinks.
